neet_phy_u14_t06_1.working: At resonance X_L = X_C, so Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2) = R.

neet_phy_u14_t06_4.working: At resonance V_L = V_C, they are opposite in phase and cancel, so the source supplies only V_R. V_L = I·X_L = Q·V can then exceed V when Q > 1. Both statements are true; R is taken as the explanation, though it is arguable since the size of V_L depends on Q.

neet_phy_u14_t06_5.working: Below resonance X_C > X_L, so the circuit is capacitive and current leads voltage: I is correct. Resonant frequency 1/sqrt(LC) does not depend on R, and higher R makes resonance broader, not sharper: II is incorrect.
